- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and forecast is falling, avoid underestimating the drop — adjust downward by 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum + negative sentiment, reduce forecast by 2–4% to account for lagged correction.  
- If forecast spikes after a recent high and sentiment is neutral or mixed, cap the spike at 10% above prior peak to prevent overreaction.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model tends to overestimate — apply a 3–5% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- If true outcome deviates >10% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust future forecast by 1–2% downward for the next 3–5 days to reflect lagged sentiment effect.
